Hi Anita — really glad the demo landed well. Short answer: both paths are possible. Quick options below so you can pick and we can get legal/ops moving.

Option A — 3-week timebox extension (no model/throughput changes)
- Fixed extension: +3 weeks from 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-05.
- Cost: USD $6,750 (est. based on current burn & reserved burst headroom).
- Process: sign a 1‑page PoC addendum (DocuSign). No change to billing cadence.

Option B — Token credit top-up (pay-as-you-go style)
- Credits: $7,000 in token credits, usable over the next 60 days.
- Pros: no amendment required; immediate provisioning of burst capacity.
- Cons: credits are consumed; no date extension guarantee.

Option C — Convert to a temporary seat-credits bundle (recommended if you expect parallel users)
- 3-seat test pack (3 seats, limited concurrency) for the remainder of the PoC: $6,000 + one small setup fee.
- Convertible: if you decide to commit at the end of the PoC we can roll a portion toward a discounted committed package.

I'll attach a short proposal (redwood-proposal-v1.pdf) with the line items. If you want the simplest legal path, Option B gets you unblocked fastest. Option A requires the addendum but gives a firm runway.

If you'd like, I can also run this by our Pricing & Contracts lead for quick approval on a one-off concession (we occasionally provide a small goodwill credit for timing slips). Let me know which option you prefer and I'll prepare the addendum or the credit invoice.

Cheers,
